claims.claim: rfc-001-sync-impersonation.md's design only impersonates the sync operation (the destination service account performs the actual apply), leaving diff/dry-run untouched by impersonation config; this produces both T-26271's in-cluster CLI diff failure (server-side diff dry-run is authorized by Kubernetes as a patch, and the impersonated destination SA lacks that patch on cluster-scoped resources like ClusterRole/cert-manager-cainjector) and T-28695's external-cluster problem (Server-Side Diff in the application-controller reconcile path ignores destinationServiceAccounts entirely and runs as the raw, deliberately least-privilege cluster-secret credential, forcing ever-broadening unbounded patch RBAC grants).

prd-progressive-sync-deletion.md's Reverse deletion strategy is designed to wait for one Application to be fully deleted before moving to the next step; T-28511 shows that when a matched Application is stuck in Progressing (deletion never completes) and is deleted manually, the applicationset-controller does not respect its Deleting status and restarts the wave from the top, producing the infinite delete/recreate loop the PRD's sequential-wait design does not account for.

rfc-002-manifest-hydrator.md's design has every dry-source commit produce a fresh hydrated commit on the syncSource branch; T-27949 shows that on repos piloting this hydrator, each such hydration commit is picked up as a resolved-source-revision change independent of the generated child Application.spec change, feeding directly into the RollingSync specChanged/Healthy-promotion timing gap that leaves child Applications OutOfSync with no new sync operation created.

rfc-002-manifest-hydrator.md establishes the commit server as the component that pushes to the hydrated/sync branch (and, per its signing design, the only component positioned to sign those pushes); T-27327's proposed rollback flow pushes directly to the sync branch outside the commit server, so when a branch's SourceIntegrity policy requires signed commits the rollback push lands unsigned and is rejected by the git host, with no messaging or retry path back to the operator.

strategy.md's roadmap explicitly scopes ordered or automated deletion of ApplicationSet-generated Applications out of rollout orchestration, leaving teardown a manual, one-Application-at-a-time operator action; T-24578 is a symptom filed directly against that scoping decision, requesting DAG-based destroy ordering across multiple ApplicationSets sharing a cluster and describing a hand-built app-of-apps workaround made necessary specifically because ApplicationSets don't support it.

rfc-001-sync-impersonation.md's design determines the impersonation service account on a per-Application basis rather than per-resource, using Application.spec.destination.namespace for the whole Application; T-27833 reports this exact granularity as the security gap, since a namespace resource committed into the same Application's manifests is applied under that same per-Application service account, letting a user bypass the intended clusterResourceWhitelist-based namespace boundary by committing a namespace object matching the allowed name pattern.
